name: DARPA Grand Challenge, autonomous desert driving
posed_evidence: DARPA prize competition announcement and event dates as stated on the Wikipedia page
statement: Can a fully autonomous ground vehicle complete a 200 kilometre off-road desert course within ten hours with no human intervention?
status_source: Wikipedia, DARPA Grand Challenge (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Grand_Challenge): no vehicle finished in March 2004; Stanford's Stanley won the 2 million dollar prize on 8 October 2005

name: DARPA Urban Challenge
posed_evidence: DARPA prize competition announcement and event dates as stated on the Wikipedia page
statement: Can an autonomous vehicle drive 96 kilometres through urban traffic obeying traffic law, merging, parking and negotiating intersections with other vehicles?
status_source: Wikipedia, DARPA Grand Challenge (2007) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Grand_Challenge_(2007)): Tartan Racing's Boss won the 2 million dollar prize on 3 November 2007

name: DARPA Network Challenge, red balloons
posed_evidence: DARPA prize competition announcement and event dates as stated on the Wikipedia page
statement: Can a team locate ten red weather balloons moored at undisclosed sites across the continental United States within a day using the internet and social networks?
status_source: Wikipedia, DARPA Network Challenge (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Network_Challenge): the MIT team found all ten balloons in under nine hours on 5 December 2009

name: DARPA Shredder Challenge
posed_evidence: DARPA prize competition announcement and event dates as stated on the Wikipedia page
statement: Can shredded documents cut into more than 10,000 pieces be reconstructed from images well enough to solve the puzzles written on them?
status_source: Wikipedia, DARPA Shredder Challenge 2011 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Shredder_Challenge_2011): the team All Your Shreds Are Belong to U.S. solved all five puzzles and won the 50,000 dollar prize in December 2011

name: DARPA UAVForge Challenge
posed_evidence: DARPA prize competition announcement and event dates as stated on the Wikipedia page
statement: Can a backpack-portable unmanned aircraft fly quietly into a site, perch and conduct three hours of surveillance, then return, built by a crowd-sourced team?
status_source: DARPA Prize Competitions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Prize_Competitions): none of the 140 teams met the technical requirements and the 100,000 dollar prize was not claimed in 2012

name: DARPA FANG Challenge

status_source: DARPA Prize Competitions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Prize_Competitions): a three-person team won 1 million dollars in April 2013; the later rounds were cancelled

status_source: DARPA Prize Competitions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Prize_Competitions): three teams won a total of 150,000 dollars in 2014

name: DARPA Chikungunya Challenge

status_source: DARPA Prize Competitions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Prize_Competitions): 500,000 dollars in prizes awarded to 11 winners on 12 May 2015

status_source: DARPA Prize Competitions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Prize_Competitions): a University of Florida team won the 2 million dollar top prize at the 2019 final

name: DARPA Subterranean Challenge

name: DARPA Launch Challenge
